decisions.mark: states that a repository's own declared index_scope is preferred, and that every failure to find one falls through to indexing the whole repository
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "It returns one of two scopes: the repo's own declared `index_scope:`, or the whole repository minus a set of subtractions." | WHY: The answer states the declared scope is used when usable, and that absent, unusable, or rejected declarations (including malformed or no usable roots) fall through to the whole-repo scope. || QUOTE: the repo's own declared `index_scope:`, or the whole repository minus a set of subtractions. ... `no index_scope: key → None → fall through` ... `present but unusable → _Rejected(reason) → WARNING, whole repo` | WHY: The answer says a declared index_scope is the first choice and shows that absent, unreadable, malformed or unusable declarations all fall through to indexing the whole repo. || QUOTE: the repo's own declared `index_scope:`, or the whole repository minus a set of subtractions; "no `index_scope:` key → None → fall through"; "present but unusable → _Rejected(reason) → WARNING, whole repo" | WHY: The answer states that a declared index_scope is used when usable, and that an absent, unusable or rejected declaration falls through to the whole repository.

decisions.mark: conveys that the fallback carries a REASON explaining which scope was used and why, so an unstated scope is never silently guessed
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The reason string always says why the whole-repo tier was chosen: either "no `index_scope:` is declared" or the specific rejection message. | WHY: The answer states the fallback scope carries a reason string explaining why it was chosen (not declared vs. rejected), and the decision tree shows `_Rejected(reason)` → WARNING, so the scope is never chosen silently. || QUOTE: The reason string always says why the whole-repo tier was chosen: either "no `index_scope:` is declared" or the specific rejection message. | WHY: The answer states the fallback carries a reason string explaining which scope was chosen and why (undeclared vs. rejected), and the decision tree shows `_Rejected(reason)` and a `DerivedScope` source label, so the scope is never silently guessed. || QUOTE: The reason string always says why the whole-repo tier was chosen: either "no `index_scope:` is declared" or the specific rejection message. | WHY: The answer states the fallback scope carries a reason explaining why it was chosen, including the not-declared case and specific rejections, so the scope is never silently guessed.
